title: Telemetry-driven quantization and prompt heuristics sprint
content:
Purpose and scope:
This sprint notebook captures our telemetry-first approach for a telecom POC: choose a quant/profile + prompt orchestration strategy that meets 99p latency <= 180ms, median latency < 60ms, and token-cost <= target (approx 0.35x baseline) while keeping answer-quality within delta BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-sim thresholds compared to the baseline float32 model.

Context and constraints:
- Customer: Tier-1 telecom (real-time agent assistant, short-turn dialog, multi-turn context up to 2k tokens)
- Target SLA: 99th <= 180ms, p50 <= 60ms, 99p tail cost must be predictable for billing forecasts.
- Deploy mode for POC: hybrid (dedicated us-west1 pool + hosted fallback), must support private KV caching in Dedicated.
- Data-sensitivity: low PII in dev eval, but later stages will be anonymized. No QAT that requires full customer data during POC.

Telemetry signals we will drive from the POC harness:
- per-request sequence length distribution (sampled at 1% of requests)
- per-token generation latency (ms/token), per-layer CPU/GPU time (when available)
- KV cache hit rate and avg prefix length used
- batch size distribution vs latency
- quantization-induced logits shift (KL divergence to float baseline on eval set)
- sampling output variability (distinct-1/2, semantic-similarity to gold)

Quick summary of decisions so far (working):
- Use a 7B family open model as baseline (float32) for quality comparison.
- Candidate quant profiles: int8-ptq (symmetric per-channel), int4-adaptive (per-tensor), and hybrid bf16-kernel (mixed). Avoid QAT for PII reasons in POC.
- Prompt orchestration: dynamic few-shot selector (select 0-3 exemplars based on intent match score) + system prompt compression (template + short context anchors).

Experiment matrix (high-level):
- Axis A: quant profile = [float32, int8-ptq, int4-adaptive, bf16-mixed]
- Axis B: KV caching = [off, prefix-only, full-kv with 8k expiry]
- Axis C: batching policy = [latency-first (max 8ms wait), throughput-first (batch window 20ms), adaptive (deadline-aware)]
- Axis D: prompt population = [0-shot, 1-shot static, dynamic-1-shot, dynamic-3-shot]
- Axis E: sampling = [greedy, top-k=40, top-p=0.95 + temp 0.8]
We will run a 48-hour sweep covering combinations prioritized by telemetry cost models (expected token savings vs latency impact).

Primary metrics (collected at request level):
- L_q: latency quantile metrics (p50, p90, p95, p99)
- C_t: cost per 1k tokens (tokens served + op cost)
- Q_delta: quality delta vs baseline (semantic-sim embedding similarity on held-out dialogs)
- KV_hit: KV cache hit rate and median prefix length
- B_inflation: batch size distribution and queue delay contribution
- KL_shift: average KL divergence of logits to float baseline for same prompts

Small example telemetry table (sample row) as plain text:
request_id | seq_len | quant | kv_mode | batch_wait_ms | gen_latency_ms | kv_hit | embedding_sim
abcd1234   | 34      | int8  | prefix   | 5             | 42             | 0.62   | 0.91

Observed early signals (first 24h sweep):
- int8-ptq + prefix-KV + latency-first batching: p50=48ms, p95=112ms, p99=176ms, embedding_sim=0.90 (delta -0.02). Cost ~0.42x baseline. KV_hit ~ 0.58. Logs show increased rare-token KL_shift concentrated in output heads for numbers/dates.
- int4-adaptive: p50=39ms, p95=140ms, p99=310ms (spiky tail), embedding_sim=0.86 (delta -0.06). Quant artifacts appeared on longer completions (>= 120 tokens), output truncation observed in 0.6% of runs.
- bf16-mixed: quality indistinguishable from float, p99 ~ 190-220ms depending on batch policy, cost ~0.82x baseline.

Interim interpretation:
- int8-ptq is a promising sweet spot for latency vs quality. int4 has unacceptable tail behavior for this latency-sensitive, multi-turn product without further model surgery or QAT. bf16 helps quality but doesn't meet the cost/latency targets.
- KV caching materially reduces per-request tokens; a conservative prefix-only policy gives the best risk/reward during POC.
- Adaptive batching provides the best cost-performance tradeoff when combined with strict deadline fallback (if queue time > 15ms, flush).

Prompt orchestration notes (experiments and heuristics):
- Dynamic few-shot selector is implemented as a lightweight intent match (embedding cosine on short schema) and reduces unnecessary exemplar tokens by ~26% vs static 3-shot baseline while maintaining similarity scores.
- System prompt compression: replace verbose role-descriptions with anchor tokens + example short function docs. Saved ~120 tokens per prompt on average.
- For agent assistant, prioritize instruction clarity over exemplars when recent conversation context length > 512 tokens. Example heuristic: if recent_context_tokens > 512 -> force 0-shot + compressed system; else consider dynamic-1-shot.

Operational runbook (short):
- Pre-sweep: snapshot model version and quant profile artifact id, log config to Confluence and JIRA-ENG-4912.
- Start sweep: run throughput-first warmup (2 hours) to populate KV cache. Enable telemetry agents with 1% request sampling to full trace capture.
- Mid-sweep: at 12h check for output artifacts (KL_shift > 0.07 or quality delta > 0.05) -> abort profile and mark for QAT follow-up.
- Post-sweep: aggregate metrics, produce decision recommendation (go/no-go), and prepare a short demo trace set for customer review.

Checklist before recommending int8 to customer:
- [ ] p99 <= 180ms sustained across 24h with production-like traffic (stress test)
- [ ] semantic-sim delta <= 0.03 on curated eval dialogs
- [ ] no observed hallucination class shifts in thresholded intent categories
- [ ] KV expiry and privacy knobs documented for Dedicated deployment
- [ ] billing forecast model updated (expected cost per 1M tokens)

Open questions and items for next sprint:
- Investigate int8 per-layer clipping to reduce rare-token KL_shift (early hypothesis: output head scales need layer-wise range calibration).
- Decide whether to offer an opt-in QAT path for specific customers with masked PII pipelines. QAT might fix int4 tail problems but operational complexity increases.
- Evaluate hardware affinity: run int8 on a different kernel (cuBLAS vs custom) to confirm kernel selection impact on p99 tail. Document in GH PR linked above.
- Telemetry: consider raising sampling to 5% for additional signal on rare tokens during final validation.

Deliverables from this sprint (expected):
- concise recommendation doc for customer (one-pager) summarizing best quant profile + prompt heuristics + ops guardrails
- telemetry dashboard snapshot (p50/p95/p99 + cost overlays) and a short runbook for Dedicated rollouts
- decision log entry (Confluence) and follow-up tickets for int8 clipping and potential QAT experiment

Notes to self / fragments:
- Watch out for tokenizers causing off-by-one that blow up tail in int4 runs.
- Add a tiny eval subset that matches telecom entities (phone numbers, RFC-styles) to stress head output.
- Add a fallback policy in routing: when p99 trending up, shift 10% of requests to bf16-mixed as live safety net for 24h before rolling back.

References and links: included in linked_artifacts above.

Status: In review with Solutions Eng lead (Hector) and Applied ML (Priya). Plan to finalize recommendation and present to customer on 2025-02-23.
